tasks.task: Work out staff needed by hour from demand data

items.when: When you have sales, covers, footfall or tickets and need staff by role for each hour or day
When the demand export first arrives, to spot gaps, closed days and odd entries
When next month's demand must be forecast from past sales, with a way to track the miss
When demand and team size are known and you need staffing levels and overload risk
When the team is a support desk and staffing follows ticket volume
When the forecast is one number, to give it a range, a base rate and a date to check it

tasks.task: Build a fair weekly rota

items.when: Every week or fortnight, to run the steps so the rota posts on time
When needs, contracts, availability and skills are in and hard shifts must be filled first
When you want two or three rota options, each with a cover and cost check, before choosing
When the team needs a repeating pattern that rotates nights and weekends fairly
When limits clash and you need a model to find the best fit within hours and budget
When the cheapest rota wins and nobody asks what it does to the people on it

tasks.task: Check a draft rota before it is published

items.when: When a manager has built next week's rota and it needs checking against rules and wage cost
When a shift may break a rest, break or overtime rule and you need the rule with its source
When a shift needs qualified people for set work and you must see if it has enough
When approved leave is in the diary, to spot critical work left with no cover
When the check quotes a scheduling law, to tie it to a dated official source

tasks.task: Write a rota rules sheet for the team

items.when: When staff keep asking when the rota comes out and how to swap or book time off
When lateness, overtime and absence rules are not written down either
Before it goes on the wall, to cut the sheet to words every shift worker would use

tasks.task: Cost a late change to a posted rota

items.when: When a manager wants to add, cut or move shifts after the rota was posted
When the change may trigger extra pay or a rest rule and you need the rule with its source
When the change looks cheap, to trace what it does to fairness and next week's cover

tasks.task: Build a reusable rota template in a spreadsheet

items.when: Before building, to fix which rules and fairness counts the sheet must show
When managers need dropdowns and validation so shifts are entered the same way each week
Before handing it over, to find formula errors and totals that do not tie

tasks.task: Build a 12-month hiring plan with full monthly cost

items.when: When each planned role needs pay, employer costs, kit and ramp time by month
When you have headcount history and want forecast, role plan and budget in one run
When leavers must be counted in, to see hires needed with a low and high range
When growth goals and a budget must become a role-by-role order to hire in
When finance needs the plan as a budget by team and month
When the budget cannot carry it all, to compare two differently shaped plans with dates
Before the plan goes to the owner, to find broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Work out the full cost of one hire

items.when: When the owner is weighing one role and wants the monthly and first-year cost, not just salary
When finance wants hire set against contractor, with a payback estimate
When it is unclear which single hire would unblock growth
When the salary line is a guess and you need public pay ranges for the role and place
Before sharing, to tie each tax and benefit rate to a source the accountant can confirm

tasks.task: Test a hiring plan against slow sales

items.when: When the plan needs base, best and worst cases and signals that say switch
When you must see if wages can be paid over the next 30, 60 and 90 days
When sales dip each year and the plan needs a dated downside case and actions
Before the plan is signed off, to imagine it failed and find the hidden assumptions
When the plan only works if everything goes right, to ask how much room for error it has

tasks.task: Build a team capacity view

items.when: When you need workload against people, who is overloaded and whether more can be taken on
When sales wants a date and you must see if the team can really meet it
When a service team's paid hours must be turned into utilisation and margin
When the answer is always more people, to look first for waiting and rework

tasks.task: Set up and keep a contractor roster and tracker

items.when: When freelancers need one roster with rates, dates, documents, access and spend
When the firm uses many contractors and needs an onboarding list and a vendor plan
When someone on the roster works like staff, to flag the status risk
Each month, to see who to keep, whose terms to fix and which agreements to redo

tasks.task: Write a brief for a freelance or contractor job

items.when: Before work starts, to set scope, deliverables, deadline, rate and who approves
When the job is judged on results and both sides need limits, help and review dates agreed
Before sending, to read the brief as the freelancer and list what they would have to ask

tasks.task: Write contractor onboarding and offboarding checklists

items.when: When each contractor needs the same start and finish steps, with access listed
When a contract ends and you need a checklist and handover tied to the end date
When the steps must be written with who does what and the edge cases

tasks.task: Write a one-page policy for using contractors

items.when: When managers hire freelancers their own way and one plain rule sheet is needed
Before writing, to learn which working patterns raise status risk
When the policy is drafted, to cut it to one page managers will read

tasks.task: Review headcount and contractor spend each quarter

items.when: In the two weeks after quarter end, to compare plan with actual and reset the next quarter
When each quarter's numbers arrive, to check the plan and name the budget gap
When leaders need headcount and leaver trends from the staff spreadsheet
When wage or contractor spend moved and each line past the limit needs a reason

tasks.task: Plan seasonal staffing from last year's numbers

items.when: As soon as peak dates are known, to work back from the first busy day
When there is still time to hire and train and you have last year's numbers
When seasonal and agency staff need tracking beside the core team
When this year's peak must be forecast before you set numbers to hire
When an online shop's peak also needs support hire dates and warehouse terms
Before committing, to imagine the peak went badly and find why

tasks.task: Write seasonal job posts and candidate messages

items.when: When you need a short clear post with dates, hours, pay and only the real requirements
When the post must stand out among other seasonal jobs and needs several opening lines
When dozens of applicants need a clear next step or a kind no
Before posting, to read it as a student or temp worker and see if dates and pay are clear

tasks.task: Plan a hiring day with a fast, fair scorecard

items.when: When many people are seen in one day and each needs the same short scorecard
When a ten-minute task would show more than an interview
When applications must be cut to an invite list scored only on job needs
When applications arrive in batches and each must be scored the same way

tasks.task: Build a two-day onboarding kit for seasonal staff

items.when: When each starter needs a pre-start list and a first-days plan
When training is a live session and must be planned minute by minute
When the tills, stock or safety steps need writing as task cards
In the first weeks, to check who has finished training and what to fix

tasks.task: Run the end-of-season survey and rehire list

items.when: When the season ends and you need who to ask back and what each was good at
When leavers should be asked a few questions and the answers read for themes
When you want to look back at which hiring steps found the people who stayed

tasks.task: Plan cover for absence, leave or a disruption

items.when: When a strike, storm or closure is coming and essential services must stay covered
When one role has no backup and each critical task needs a trained second person
When one person's leave needs a cover map and task-by-task notes

tasks.task: Report wage cost against sales and budget

items.when: When dated shift and sales records need a monthly summary with traceable totals
When wage cost moved against last period and each line needs a written reason
When you want quick charts of hours and sales by day from an upload

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real firm, its contracts, rules and budget
Whenever the work states a legal rule or a cost rate, to give it a dated source or cut it
Before any rota or cost sheet leaves your hands, to find broken formulas and wrong totals

helpers.when: When the plan says hire and the roles need posts, sourcing and screening
When rota hours feed payroll or pay rates and overtime need checking
When a rota rule, contract term or contractor status needs a policy answer
When the headcount plan must tie into the company budget and forecast
When the rota or cost model needs a robust workbook the client can keep using
When staffing depends on changing how the work itself is done

gaps: No library item checks a rota against rest, break and advance-notice rules by country; the rules item answers one question at a time
No library item costs a late schedule change, with any extra pay owed
No library item turns shop or cafe sales by hour into staff needed by role; the capacity planner is general
No library item builds a reusable rota spreadsheet with fairness counts for late and weekend shifts
No library item builds a seasonal staffing plan from last year's numbers or a rehire list
No library item plans a high-volume hiring day with slots, stations and same-day offers
No library item builds a one or two day onboarding kit for temporary staff
No library item writes a contractor brief or reviews contractor spend against quality
No library item lists and removes a contractor's system access when the work ends
No library item works out the full monthly cost of a hire with employer taxes for a named country
No library item reports wage cost as a share of sales or builds a skills and cross-training matrix
No library item makes clearly different versions of a seasonal job post to choose between
The library has no tool guide for rota or scheduling software
